steps.body: To check a long sum, re-add it in a DIFFERENT order — front-to-back the first time, back-to-front the second. Matching totals is powerful evidence.
steps.narration: To check a long sum, re-add it in a DIFFERENT order — front-to-back the first time, back-to-front the second. Matching totals is powerful evidence.

widget.prompt: Backward check: starting from the back pair's 29, hop the remaining ten-addend.

commonLandings.feedback: One step is a single one — the remaining addend is a whole ten.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop adds 10. From 29, 1 hops land on 39.
widget.successFeedback: 39 — the backward path lands with the forward one, and the sum is confirmed.

predict.prompt: Forward gave 84; backward gives 84. What did you learn?

options.label: Strong evidence the sum is right

predict.reveal: Two independent paths agreeing is exactly what a correct total looks like.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2n check.
invariants: Regrouping addends changes the ORDER of joining, never the total — every staging of the sum must land on the same number for g2n check.
misconceptions: Believing the grouping or order of addends can change a sum, or letting an addend join twice or not at all while restaging.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which single change to the staging would actually change the total — and which only changes the path?

commonErrors.feedback: The backward path starts 11 + 24 — pairing with 36 skips an addend's turn.

widget.prompt: You add 17 + 25 + 3 as (17 + 3) + 25. Is the total allowed to change?

options.label: No — regrouping addends never changes a sum
options.feedback: Correct — addition lets you group in any order; 20 + 25 and the left-to-right path both reach 45.

options.label: Yes — the parentheses add extra
options.feedback: Parentheses only choose which pair goes first; they contribute nothing of their own.

options.label: Only if the answer stays under 20
options.feedback: The regrouping freedom has no size limit — it is a property of addition itself.

options.label: Yes — 3 must always join last
options.feedback: That treats position as a rule, but addends own no fixed turn — 17 + 3 first is exactly the friendly-pair move.
